Working notes — push angle selection

Evidence so far (10 days, one push/day):
- B "quality story": pushed days 1,2,3,9,10. Day-1+2 report: 2 of 2 landed — the best result seen. Day-10 report: 1 of 2 landed. So B is the only angle with confirmed landings; it is also the safest, no timing/discount dependence.
- C "limited-time urgency": days 4,5. Day-6 report: 0 of 2 landed. No confirmed success.
- D "customer testimonial": days 6,7,8. Day-8 report: 0 of 2 landed. No confirmed success.
- A "price cut": never tried.

Analytics caveat: reports only ever cover "the last 2 pushes" with no per-day breakdown, so single-day attribution is unreliable. Day-4 report (0 of 2) covers days 3–4, which conflicts with B's earlier success — treat B as historically best, not guaranteed.

Signals to ignore: unsubscribes (days 2, 7, 10) and "no deliverability complaints" notes do not track any angle; they've appeared before good and bad reports alike. Legal sign-off on all four angles is standard — not a constraint.

Decision rule going forward:
- Default to B (quality story) unless new evidence contradicts it.
- Deprioritize C and D until a report shows them landing.
- A remains untested; only test it if B's landing rate drops.
- Stop rotating angles on a schedule; the evidence does not support rotation.
